summary: One run resolves the control's question if it is read from the Triton kernel's own us and the paired-vs-SGLang ratio on unpooler decode_32, calibrated by the byte-identical decode_16 row in the same run, not from the +-4% cross-run attribution: Triton-kernel rows reproduce within ~1% across runs (pooler rows 20.2/20.4, 20.5/20.5, 25.2/25.4 us; paired ratios within 0.6%), so the 10% m=32 penalty the parent measured (19.8 us vs 18.0 us for identical weight bytes) is far above noise. A clear gain is unambiguous; a flat result is ambiguous but no cheap companion disambiguates it better than running this first, so no companions.
justification: Mechanism, corrected against the parent's actual rows: the parent did NOT lose at m=16. Its BLOCK_N=64 / 16-step kernel streamed the 67.1 MB unpooler in 18.0 us (3.73 TB/s, paired speedup 1.033 vs nvjet 18.3-19.1 us) where the pooler's BLOCK_N=32 / 32-step kernel does 20.2-20.5 us (3.3 TB/s) on the same bytes; so the plain-Triton 'ceiling' the earlier review assumed is already broken by this tile, and the only unpooler problem left is the m=32 row: 19.8 us kernel, paired 0.973, a +10% penalty over m=16 for the same weight traffic (the pooler shows +24%: 25.4 vs 20.5). The control changes exactly one thing, the M tiling at m>16 (two [16,64] accumulators and two tl.dot per K-step against one weight tile), with smem, FLOPs, x bytes and the K-step order unchanged, so numerics are row-for-row identical to the parent and the diff is attributable to codegen of the 32-row dot. Expected rows are consistent with TASK.md: unpooler decode_32 has weight 62 and is ~30% of the decode_32 load, floor 14.1 us; a full fix (19.8 -> 18.0) is ~+2.8% on that load, ~+0.9% on the geomean, inside the +-1.5% CI, so the headline cannot be the readout, the per-row kernel us and paired ratio must be. Weakest link: the hypothesis frames a dichotomy (32-row tl.dot tile vs streaming bandwidth) that does not exhaust the mechanisms, and the control removes less than it claims. At the ISA level a [32,64] mma.sync dot is two [16,64] dots sharing B fragments; the two-dot form keeps the same mma count, the same ldmatrix of x, the same cp.async fill (48 KB/stage) and the same 2x x re-read from L2 (128 programs x 256 KB = 32 MB at m=32 vs 16 MB at m=16; pooler: 64 MB vs 32 MB, matching the ordering of the penalties 24% > 10%). What it can change is Triton's warp layout ([2,2] -> [1,4]-style, which halves per-warp duplicate B-fragment reads from smem) and whether the compiler shares the w ldmatrix across the two dots (not guaranteed; the x operand of each dot is distinct, the B operand the same). So a flat result does not 'confirm the bandwidth ceiling on a second shape' as the Risk section says; it says the penalty is not the dot's M-shape, leaving x-traffic amplification, issue-rate (4 warps doing 2x mma+ldmatrix per step) and pipeline depth all open. The hypothesis's withdrawal clause for the whole family on a flat result is an over-inference and should not be acted on: the m=16 row already shows this kernel beating nvjet.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (landed, in the build base): inert on the two rows that can move; the parent already replaces _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl on unpooler 9<=m<=32 and the control keeps that routing, so the measured delta vs the parent is independent of it.

router-hilo-at-m8 and router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m (landed on master, ABSENT from the build base fbfb795 which descends from d2840d0 on the parity base): different layer, own CUDA graphs, no shared kernel or memory; they cannot move the unpooler rows, but the headline will sit near 1.00 like the parent's 1.0053 and is not comparable to BEST 1.151x. Promotion of a gain needs a rebase onto master and a fresh run.

pooler-triton-skinny-m32 (parent of the parent, unpromoted, in the build base): shares @triton.jit _pooler_skinny_kernel. If the implementer adds a constexpr (e.g. TWO_TILES) to that shared kernel, every pooler specialization and the unpooler m<=16 specialization recompile under a new cache key; same code, but the 'byte-for-byte identical binary' claim for the decode_16 in-run control weakens. Its pooler decode_32 loss (0.888) stays in the headline either way and must be attributed away.

Within the parent itself: unpooler decode_16 and decode_32 are different graphs and different m; the control's decode_16 row is a drift calibrator (expect ~18.0 us), not a same-shape A/B, so the m=32 readout is kernel_us(m=32)/kernel_us(m=16) in the same run (parent: 19.8/18.0 = 1.10) against the parent's ratio.
interference: Noise: the +-4% cross-run swings the prompt cites are on cuBLAS split-K rows (qkv_gate nvjet 10.8 -> 9.5 us between runs while SGLang's own time moved too); Triton-kernel rows reproduce within ~1% across the pooler run and the parent run (20.2/20.4, 20.5/20.5, 25.2/25.4 us; paired ratios 1.059/1.058, 1.063/1.057, 0.894/0.888), and err_ns on these rows is 40-60 ns (0.3%). The effect under test is 19.8 vs 18.0 us (10%), so one run resolves it: decision rule, m=32 kernel us <= 18.6 (ratio to the in-run m=16 row <= 1.03) -> the 32-row dot codegen was the penalty, adopt BLOCK_M=16 tiles across the skinny family; >= 19.4 (ratio >= 1.08) -> not the tile; 18.6-19.4 -> partial, UNSURE. ab-revert: not applicable, no landed hypothesis touches the unpooler 9..32 path and the router changes are absent from the build base anyway. ab-tune: the pooler tile has no effect on unpooler rows. control: a gain is unambiguous on its own, so by the stated criterion no companion is warranted now. The one control that would disambiguate a FLAT result (issue-rate vs bandwidth) is num_warps=8 at the m=32 specialization only, same smem and tiles; it is a one-constant change and should be queued only if this run comes back flat, not spent in parallel, because its interpretation depends on this run's answer.
rules_flags: No rule risk beyond the parent's, which passed: fp32 accumulate / bf16 store as cuBLAS and SGLang; weights used as stored; nothing derived from data cached (warmup on synthetic zeros, weight-shape-only gate); no host syncs; the only in-graph allocation is the fixed-shape torch.empty((m, 8192)) the parent already does.

Latent correctness, not rules: the two-tile path is live for every m in 17..31 but no judge test or timed shape exercises 16<m<32 (tests are m=5/130/1000 for unpooler), and the warmup uses zeros, so a mask bug on rows >= m in the second tile would go uncaught; keep the mask exactly offs_m2 = 16 + tl.arange(0,16) < M on both the load and the store.
Keep BLOCK_M=16 as the minimum dot M (tl.dot requires >= 16); do not try BLOCK_M=8 variants here.
open_questions: Implement the two-tile path as a separate @triton.jit kernel (not a new constexpr on _pooler_skinny_kernel) so the pooler specializations and the unpooler m<=16 specialization are literally the parent's binaries and the decode_16 row is a true in-run control.

Readout: judge on top_kernels us for unpooler decode_32 vs decode_16 in the same run (parent 19.8 vs 18.0) and on the paired speedup (parent 0.973 vs 1.033), not on the attribution delta vs the parent's medians (19.27/17.97) which carries the +-4% cross-run noise; record 67.1 MB / kernel us as the family's bandwidth datapoint (the m=16 row is 3.73 TB/s, already above nvjet).

If flat: the penalty is not the dot's M-shape; the remaining candidates are x re-read amplification from L2 (32 MB at m=32 vs 16 MB at m=16 for 128 programs), 4-warp issue rate on 2x mma+ldmatrix per step, and pipeline depth; queue a num_warps=8-at-m=32 control next. Do not withdraw the o-/qkv-gate siblings on a flat result here: the qkv-gate regression (BLOCK_N=16, 22-26 us vs 14 us cuBLAS) is a BLOCK_N / program-count problem, not an m=32 tile problem.

If gain: unpooler decode_16 and decode_32 both beat nvjet by ~3%; the gain only reaches the board after rebasing the parent + control onto master (router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m is not in the build base) and a fresh run; also revisit the pooler with BLOCK_N=64 (64 programs) or BLOCK_M=16 tiles, since the parent's data say the pooler's 3.3 TB/s is the BLOCK_N=32 / 32-step tile, not a Triton ceiling.
Frontmatter says base: master while depends_on names the parent; confirm churn.py bases on fbfb795 (the parent's impl_commit) as the prompt states, otherwise the comparison rows are wrong.
